The Road to the Borgo Pass

Jonathan Harker's journey from Munich to the Count's door, 1–5 May, traced from his own journal.

by railway by diligence by the Count's calèche

Railway lines are drawn through the junctions a traveller of 1893 would have passed; Stoker names only the cities. The close-up of the Borgo Pass is drawn from 30-metre terrain (Copernicus); the diligence follows the valley floor up to the saddle, and the calèche goes on "to the far side of the Pass", turns "sharply to the right" and climbs to the highest crag within reach. The castle is Stoker’s, not a real building. Relief from the Amenti atlas ground; rivers from Natural Earth.
